key_insight: Increasing Y substitution in BCFZY perovskite cathodes modestly improves predicted proton transport at 500 °C, with gas conditions strongly influencing the transport mechanism.
engineering_relevance: The findings guide protonic ceramic fuel cell cathode design—not solar cells—by linking Y content and operating atmosphere to proton conductivity.
method: Compare BCFZ, BCFZY0.1, and BCFY compositions.
Use ab initio molecular dynamics to estimate proton tracer diffusivity.
Model hydration, oxidation, and hydride formation to predict proton concentrations.
evidence_signal: From BCFZ to BCFY at 500 °C, calculations predict 1.7% higher proton diffusivity and, under PCFC operating gases, 3.8% higher proton concentration and 5.3% higher proton conductivity.
watch_item: The predicted gains depend on gas conditions; larger experimental enhancements under reducing conditions may involve a shift from hydroxyl-mediated to hydride-mediated transport.
paper_title: Effects of Yttrium doping on Proton Conductivity in Ba(Fe, Co, Zr, Y)O$_{3-δ}$ Cathode Materials for Proton Ceramic Fuel Cells
